how: About 2,500 young adults in Southern California were asked about vaping THC oil or dabs. The link held after allowing for nicotine vaping, cigarettes and smoked cannabis.
Even people who hadn't vaped cannabis in over 6 months reported more symptoms. So something else about them may explain part of the link.
The survey didn't record which products people vaped, and it ran into the 2019 outbreak of vaping lung injury (EVALI). So it can't say if those products played a part.
A 2024 review found no study that followed people who vape cannabis over time.

how: Memory and balance got worse after use in both groups, with no clear gap between them. There was no session without cannabis to compare.
The concentrate group already used concentrates far more often. More tolerance might explain why they didn't feel higher, the authors suggest, but that wasn't tested.
A review for Colorado found only 54 of 452 studies looked directly at concentrates and health. The typical strength studied was well below what's sold now.
Another review linked stronger plant cannabis, like skunk, to psychosis. Its studies of concentrates and mental health were rated poor. They asked people once, and disagreed.
